title: AppShell's nav-link table contradicts the stylesheet and its own accessibility section
foundBy: an independent reviewer agent, one of three asked whether each component specification still describes the component that exists

evidence.verified: `npx vitest run --project browser src/components/AppShell.nav.test.tsx`: 6 tests pass, one of them tabbing to a nav link with the browser's own keyboard and reading `outline-style: solid` with an `outline-color` equal to a `var(--color-accent)` probe. Removing the rule fails that test with `expected 'auto' to be 'solid'`, which is the browser default the table used to promise. Against `--color-header-bg` the ring measures 10.73:1 in the dark theme and 3.28:1 in the light one, where `--color-accent` is the darker `#0f766e`, so both clear the 3:1 WCAG 2.2 asks of a focus indicator. `npm run ci` exits 0 with every gate run, and the rule reaches the published build at `dist/styles/components/app-shell.css:191`.

details:
`components/AppShell.md:127` gives a hovered nav link `color: var(--color-text-inverse)` over `background: var(--color-nav-hover)`, and `:128` gives an active one `color: var(--color-accent)` over the same background.

`src/styles/components/app-shell.css:97` paints the active background with `color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-accent) 22%, transparent)`, and `:159` gives idle links `var(--color-header-text-muted)`. The tokens named in the States table have no effect on nav links.

The same document states the real values at `:149`, so it contradicts itself and a reader cannot tell which half is current. A brand layer re-theming the header from the States table changes tokens that do nothing, and misses the ones that do.

The table also promises a focus ring at `:129`. `app-shell.css` contains no `:focus` or `:focus-visible` rule at all, so a keyboard user gets the browser's default outline rather than the documented treatment.

notes.text: Found by the same review that produced CUI-032 through CUI-047, and missed when those records were written. Filed here so the review's findings are complete. Session agent confirmed every citation against the tree at 0ef7ea4.

The states table is corrected, in f4ea7c5. It now names `--color-header-text-muted` for an idle link and the accent `color-mix` for an active one, which is what `app-shell.css` paints and what the document's own accessibility section already said.

The focus half is left open. `app-shell.css` still has no `:focus` or `:focus-visible` rule, so the table now says a keyboard user gets the browser default. Whether the header should carry a focus ring of its own, and what it should look like, is a design decision rather than a correction.

Closed. Nav links now take the focus ring six other component sheets already use, `outline: .125rem solid var(--color-accent)` at `.125rem` offset, so the header stops being the one place a keyboard user gets the browser default.

The accent was chosen over `--color-header-text` because it is the house ring and the header already paints its title in the accent. The light theme is the tight case at 3.28:1, since the header background stays dark in both themes while the accent darkens.
